diagnoses.label: amount_tier_misrouted_to_tabular_column_header_or_subtotal_on_074
diagnoses.general_pattern: On receipts whose line-item table uses the word 'Total' or 'Amount' as a column header (e.g. 'Total(RM)' / 'Amount TX'), a naive scan for TOTAL/AMOUNT keywords picks up the per-line-item amount column cell as if it were the summary total, bypassing the true GRAND/NET/TOTAL summary line.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Selecting the first (or last) line whose canonicalized text contains TOTAL or AMOUNT, without excluding lines that are tabular column headers co-occurring with DESCRIPTION/ITEM/QTY/PRICE tokens, and without walking strict keyword tiers from most specific to least specific.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 074.jpg prediction amount '702.00' is marked amount_correct=false in field_feedback; the receipt image is an IKEA TAX INVOICE whose only summary totals are 'Total RM Including GST 6% 538.00', 'Total Rounded 538.00'; the only '702' candidate on the receipt would require combining or misreading tabular tokens or payment lines. date_correct=true shows the agent located the receipt body correctly, so the failure is specific to the amount-selection step choosing the wrong token/line.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Walk the task's declared tier priority (GRAND TOTAL > TOTAL RM / TOTAL: RM > TOTAL AMOUNT > TOTAL / AMOUNT / ...), skipping lines that are column headers (co-occur with DESCRIPTION/ITEM/QTY/U.PRICE/PRICE) and skipping lines after a tax/GST summary cutoff, and only accept a candidate whose own text yields a parseable two-decimal monetary token.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Apply receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation: normalize lines once, detect GST/TAX summary cutoff, iterate the declared tiers in order, filter out column-header lines and exclusion-keyword lines, iterate surviving candidates last-to-first and accept the first with a parseable monetary token under monetary_two_decimal_invariant.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Only receipt-style OCR tasks that declare an explicit keyword priority list and exclusion list; applies after Tesseract OCR and before writing the amount cell.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Non-receipt documents, free-text extraction, or tasks that do not declare a keyword tier structure; do not import this exclusion into openai-vision, pdf, video-frame-extraction, or unrelated xlsx guidance.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts → Mechanism anchor: receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation

diagnoses.label: amount_ocr_digit_confusable_not_normalized_on_077
diagnoses.general_pattern: Tesseract substitutes letters for digits inside the amount token on noisy receipts (O/o/Q→0, l/I/|→1, S→5, B→8, u→0), producing a candidate like '23.26' that is one leading-digit substitution away from the true printed value; without a scoped confusable-normalization pass over the amount token, the first-pass regex locks in the corrupted value.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Trusting the first monetary regex hit on the keyword line as-is, without re-parsing the candidate under digit-confusable substitutions when the surrounding context (subtotal, tax, payment, change) indicates arithmetic inconsistency.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 077.jpg prediction amount '23.26' is marked amount_correct=false while date_correct=true. The receipt (Banh Mi CafE) prints 'Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26' and 'TOTAL: 23.25' after a -0.01 rounding adjustment; the agent chose the pre-rounding value instead of the rounded TOTAL line. This is a tier-ordering/rounding-adjacency decision inside the amount-selection step, not a Tesseract failure.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: When both a 'Total (Inclusive of GST)' line and a later 'TOTAL:' line (with an intervening 'Rounding Adj') are present, prefer the final post-rounding TOTAL line as the higher-priority candidate within the TOTAL tier, and corroborate via the arithmetic cross-check (subtotal+tax±rounding = chosen total).
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Combine receipt_total_keyword_priority_disambiguation (walk last-to-first within surviving candidates) with ocr_amount_normalization_and_arithmetic_crosscheck (prefer candidates consistent with subtotal + tax − discount ± rounding when both are reliably parsed).
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Receipts that print both a pre-rounding and a post-rounding total line with an explicit 'Rounding Adj' between them; applies only when both subtotal/tax or rounding are reliably parsed.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Receipts with only a single total line, or tasks that do not require two-decimal monetary output; do not apply confusable substitutions to free text, invoice IDs, phone numbers, or dates.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts → Mechanism anchor: ocr_amount_normalization_and_arithmetic_crosscheck

diagnoses.label: null_contract_violated_by_empty_string_writeback_on_078
diagnoses.general_pattern: When the task contract declares that a failed extraction must be written as null, routing the extraction failure through a formatted string (default '', 'None', or f"{value}") produces an empty-string cell that is a distinct value from a true empty cell and fails line-by-line comparison against an oracle that uses None.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Assigning the empty string '' (or any string coercion of None) to the openpyxl total_amount cell when amount extraction fails, instead of assigning Python None directly.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 078.jpg prediction row has date '2017-02-02' and total_amount '' (empty string) in the predictions table, and amount_correct=false in field_feedback. The receipt (Thai Delicious Restaurant) clearly prints 'Grand Total : 92.80' which the keyword priority would select; the empty-string value together with date_correct=true indicates the amount path hit a parse failure branch and wrote '' instead of None (or alternatively picked no candidate and defaulted to '').
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: On any failed-extraction branch for the total_amount column, return Python None from the extraction function and assign that None directly to the openpyxl cell; never coerce through f-string, str(), or default to ''. Separately, re-run tier walking on this receipt so Grand Total is actually captured.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Apply null_vs_empty_string_contract in image-ocr and the Preserving null vs empty string on writeback note in xlsx; verify in the delivery contract self-check that cells intended as null satisfy cell.value is None.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Tasks whose contract explicitly distinguishes null from empty string in output cells (receipt-extraction task family in this packet).
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Tasks where '' is an acceptable sentinel, or formatted financial models where empty strings do not appear; do not retroactively null out legitimately-extracted zero values.
diagnoses.target_section: Preserving null vs empty string on writeback (and Delivery contract verification for data-only xlsx outputs)

diagnoses.label: date_label_binding_or_locale_disambiguation_failure_on_034
diagnoses.general_pattern: Receipts contain multiple date-like tokens (transaction date, print timestamp, closing/loyalty date) and dates printed as DD/MM/YYYY in a Malaysian locale can be misparsed as MM/DD/YYYY when the first component is ≤12, producing a swapped month/day without any ambiguity in the OCR text.
diagnoses.wrong_approach: Taking the first regex-matching date-shaped token and parsing it under an implicit MM/DD/YYYY assumption (or picking the wrong labeled line) without binding to a DATE / INVOICE DATE / 'Date:' label and without resolving locale from unambiguous rows in the batch.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: 034.jpg prediction date is '2018-08-09' with date_correct=false (amount_correct=true at 332.30). The receipt (Perniagaan Zheng Hui) prints 'Date: 09/03/2018' next to the labeled Date field; parsing this as MM/DD/YYYY yields 2018-08-09 (the prediction), while parsing under the Malaysian DD/MM/YYYY convention supported elsewhere in this batch (18/01/2018, 15/06/2017, 30/03/2018, 29-10-2017, 20-02-18, 19/02/2018, 26/02/18, 21/02/18, etc.) yields a different month. The failure is a locale-binding error, not an OCR error.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Infer the dominant day/month ordering from unambiguous rows in the batch (any row whose first component exceeds 12 fixes DD/MM) and apply it to ambiguous rows; prefer lines whose canonicalized text contains DATE/INVOICE DATE (or OCR variants DATA/DAIE) and that are not preceded by PRINT/CLOSED/CLOSING/FRN/LOYALTY/PROMO.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Apply receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale: parse under the batch-inferred (or task-declared) locale, bind to a DATE label, and emit ISO 8601. Reserve receipt_date_lenient_parse for cases where the strict regex fails.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Receipt-style OCR tasks where multiple dates may appear and where a locale convention can be inferred from unambiguous batch rows or declared by the task prompt.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Tasks with a single unambiguous date or where the locale is explicitly declared differently; do not override an unambiguous row based on batch majority.
diagnoses.target_section: Structured Field Extraction from Receipts → Mechanism anchor: receipt_date_label_binding_and_locale

diagnoses.label: iteration_budget_exhausted_without_skill_invocation_meta_signal

diagnoses.wrong_approach: Iterating per-image with repeated OCR variant sweeps and ad-hoc fixes, without consolidating per-image evidence into a small set of pattern-level edits applied in one pass.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: execution_metadata.termination_reason='max_iterations', acp_stop_reason='max_turn_requests', iteration_limit_hits=1, n_skill_invocations=0, response_tool_call_counts {terminal:27, think:22, file_editor:16} over 65 iterations with final reward 0.0 (binary) / 0.909 field accuracy.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: Run a single diagnostic pass that dumps, per image, per-variant OCR slices around keywords and the candidate (tier,value,anchor) list; then plan a small consolidated set of pattern/variant edits and re-run once.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Apply the Workflow note: batch-diagnostic-then-batch-edit from the current candidate's receipt overlay; this is a workflow-shape note, not a new mechanism anchor.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Batch OCR extraction tasks over N images with a shared heuristic pipeline.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Single-image analysis, interactive debugging tasks, or tasks where per-image state genuinely diverges.
